successCriteria.description: LeaveDetailPage accepts an employeeService prop and, on mount, fetches the signed-in profile via employeeService.getMe() to derive role and id (never decoding the JWT), computing isOwner = profile.id === request.employeeId.

The page renders ONLY the actions returned by getAvailableLeaveActions(request.status, profile.role, isOwner); an action the user may not take is not rendered at all (e.g. owner of a DRAFT sees submit/cancel and no approve/reject; a manager on a SUBMITTED request sees approve/reject and no submit/cancel).

Each rendered action button invokes the matching leaveService method (submit/approve/reject/cancel) with only the request id, and on success updates local state with the returned LeaveRequestView so the displayed status reflects the new state without a manual reload.
On action failure the API's error message is surfaced (err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Something went wrong') in a role='alert' element.
The approval-comment row is omitted entirely when approvalComment is null (no dash/empty placeholder rendered).
App.tsx passes the already-available employeeService into <LeaveDetailPage leaveService={leaveService} employeeService={employeeService} /> so the page compiles and is deployable.

A new LeaveDetailPage.test.tsx covers: owner sees submit/cancel for DRAFT and no approve/reject; manager sees approve/reject for SUBMITTED and no submit/cancel; a forbidden action is not rendered; a successful action updates displayed status without reload; a failed action surfaces the API error; the approval-comment row is absent when null.

constraints: Role awareness must come from employeeService.getMe() (GET /employees/me); never decode the JWT to obtain role or id.
approve/reject take NO comment input and no body; the buttons must not collect or send a comment.
Action availability is determined exclusively by getAvailableLeaveActions(status, role, isOwner) from modules/leave; do not re-implement the role/status matrix inline.
Action buttons must not be rendered for actions the user may not take; render only the returned action set.
The page must not prescribe HTTP methods/paths or component/field names beyond what already exists; the code agent chooses implementation shape.
outOfScope: Backend/API changes to the leave workflow endpoints or their authorization logic — this phase is presentation-only and consumes the existing service methods.
Adding a comment input or body to approve/reject — the backend takes no body and the buttons must not collect a comment.
Decoding the JWT or any client-side auth logic for role/identity — role awareness comes solely from getMe().

entityInvariants.invariant: Accepts both leaveService and employeeService; on mount loads the leave request and the signed-in profile, derives isOwner, and renders only the actions permitted by getAvailableLeaveActions for the current status/role/ownership.

After a successful action, the page's displayed request is replaced by the LeaveRequestView returned from the service call, so status reflects the new state without reload; approvalComment null renders no comment row.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Returns the authenticated employee's profile (id + role); must be the sole source of role awareness.
Owner-only action; returns the updated LeaveRequestView.
Manager/Admin action; takes no comment/body; returns the updated LeaveRequestView.
Manager/Admin action; takes no comment/body; returns the updated LeaveRequestView.
Owner action; returns the updated LeaveRequestView.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Reuse getAvailableLeaveActions(status, role, isOwner) exactly as exported from modules/leave (leave.actions.ts) to compute the action set; do not duplicate its matrix.
Match the ILeaveService method signatures (submit/approve/reject/cancel take only id and return Promise<LeaveRequestView>); approve/reject accept no body/comment.
Match IEmployeeService.getMe(): Promise<EmployeeProfile> and EmployeeProfile.id/role for ownership and role awareness.
Use LeaveStatus, EmployeeRole, and LeaveRequestView (employeeId, status, approvalComment) as defined; approvalComment null must omit the row.

Follow the existing test conventions (vitest + @testing-library/react, MemoryRouter/Routes/Route, vi.fn() service mocks, ApiError for failures, getByRole('alert')/getByRole('button', { name }) queries).
Surface errors using the existing pattern err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Something went wrong' in a role='alert' element.

integrationPoints.why: Determines which action buttons to render based on status, role, and ownership.
Provides the signed-in profile (id + role) for ownership and role awareness.
Executes the workflow actions and returns the updated LeaveRequestView.
Must pass employeeService into LeaveDetailPage so the page compiles and is deployable.
